clue.text: Generous, so deliver a few

parts.note: to deliver something is to hand it over
a few means some

explanation.surface: A generous person hands out a few of whatever is going.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome sum or gift is a liberal, ample one.

clue.text: Very warm neck-wear used in bed

parts.note: hot means very warm
a tie is worn round the neck

explanation.surface: Someone wears a warm tie to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hottie' is informal British for a hot-water bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot-water bottle warms the sheets before sleep.

clue.text: Nothing the knight should follow

indicators.note: follow places the word for should after the chess letter

parts.note: N is the chess abbreviation for knight
ought means should

explanation.surface: A medieval knight is told what to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Nought is zero or nil.

clue.text: Ox young Edward guided

parts.note: a steer is a young castrated ox
Ed is a short, familiar form of Edward

explanation.surface: Young Edward led an ox along.
explanation.definitionFit: Steered means directed or piloted.

clue.text: Amount Ernie coughed up to support bonington, for example

indicators.note: coughed up suggests the letters spluttered out in a jumble

explanation.surface: Ernie pays a sum to sponsor an expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coughed up' rearranges AMOUNT ERNIE. Chris Bonington is a famous British climber of Everest and Annapurna.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonington is an example of a climber of high peaks.

clue.text: Hazardously bash in then drive away

indicators.note: done hazardously, the letters of bash in are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone recklessly breaks in a door and then flees in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazardously' rearranges the letters of BASH IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish someone is to expel or send them away.

clue.text: While generations turn over, I locate a weapon

parts.note: as can mean while

indicators.note: turn over says the word for generations is flipped back to front

parts.note: ages are generations

explanation.surface: Over the generations, someone tracks down an old weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender iron-tipped spear used in southern Africa.

clue.text: I told ray about paganism

indicators.note: about indicates the letters of I told ray are turned around and mixed

explanation.surface: Someone reports Ray's pagan beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Paganism involves the worship of images or false gods.

clue.text: Student residence by the railway inn

parts.note: a hostel houses students
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A student hall stands near the railway pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostelry is an old word for a pub or tavern.

clue.text: Pillars, spirit and water found in Texas

indicators.note: the spirit and water are placed inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: TX is the postal abbreviation for Texas
rum is a spirit
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: A drinker finds rum and water in Texas, propped up on pillars.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumeau is a stone pillar or section of wall between two openings, as in a church doorway.

clue.text: Neckties worn in town square

parts.note: Ascot is a town in Berkshire, England, famous for its racecourse
S is used as an abbreviation for square

explanation.surface: Smart neckties are seen on men in a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is an English town known for its royal race meeting, where the tie of the same name was once fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a broad cravat-style tie, so the plural names several such neckwear items.

clue.text: When in it she might succeed

indicators.note: read as 'when she is in in it', placing the pronoun inside the two little words

parts.note: taken as written
her stands for she, the object form of the pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman hopes to make a success of something once she is involved in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' is the container signal: read the clue as 'when she is in in it'. 'Might' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to succeed to a title or estate after its previous holder.

clue.text: Related to fly in Columbia's eastern environment

indicators.note: an environment surrounds, so the other letters go around the insect

parts.note: CO is the country code for Colombia, here spelt Columbia
a gnat is a small fly

explanation.surface: A biologist links a fly to the eastern habitat of a South American country.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognate words or languages are akin, sharing a common origin.

clue.text: 'The da Vinci code', for instance

parts.note: the novel's title is read literally as a cipher devised by Leonardo

explanation.definitionFit: A cryptogram or cipher text is written in a secret code.

clue.text: Newspaper displays a cleaner image

parts.note: a daily is a British term for a cleaning woman who comes in each day
a mirror image is a reflection

explanation.surface: A newspaper story shows a cleaner's reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'daily' is a domestic cleaner; the answer is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Mirror is a long-running British tabloid paper.

clue.text: Rather odd kind of street keeper

parts.note: a ranger is a forest or park keeper

explanation.surface: A park warden on the street seems somewhat peculiar.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative means more peculiar than another.

clue.text: Marks again, and rewrites the notes

explanation.surface: A teacher remarks and rewrites the notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Marking a test once more, or rearranging a piece of music for new instruments, are both re-scoring.

clue.text: General tendency for me to be a fashion director

parts.note: a trend is a general tendency
the crossword's compiler calls himself the setter

explanation.surface: A setter fancies himself a style leader following the general tendency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Me' is the setter of the crossword speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leads others in style and dress is the person who starts a craze.

clue.text: Divide the underworld group

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and the realm itself
a sect is a religious group

explanation.surface: A gang from the underworld splits up.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissect is to cut apart for examination.

clue.text: Our dean composed a lovely poem

indicators.note: composed means the letters of our dean are put together in a fresh order

explanation.surface: The college dean writes a pleasing verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a short poem with a refrain, a pleasing lyric form.

clue.text: Replacement judge accepts perjury

indicators.note: accepts means the word for judge takes the lie inside it

parts.note: ref, short for referee, is a judge in sport
perjury is telling a lie under oath

explanation.surface: A substitute judge turns a blind eye to false testimony.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief is a stand-in who takes over a duty from another.

clue.text: Pamela terminates some small beetle

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Pamela kills off a small beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaters are click beetles, which flip themselves up with a snap.

clue.text: Charger accrues anyway

indicators.note: anyway suggests the letters of accrues in any order at all

explanation.surface: A charging cavalry horse builds up speed regardless.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who charges another with an offence brings an accusation.

clue.text: Male fish is well bred

parts.note: a gent is a man
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A male fish is said to have refined breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Genteel means polite and refined, of good social standing.

clue.text: Reg ran around to collect things

indicators.note: around tells us to move the letters of Reg ran about

explanation.surface: Reg ran about town gathering odds and ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To garner is to gather or store up.

clue.text: Renovating process to the front of the elevator

parts.note: the face is the front of something
a lift is the British word for an elevator

explanation.surface: An overhaul is applied to the front panel of the elevator.
explanation.definitionFit: A facelift is a cosmetic renovation, of a face or figuratively of a building.

clue.text: I relax about special exam retakes

indicators.note: about means the word for relax is placed round the letter I

parts.note: to rest is to relax

explanation.surface: A student unwinds before facing a second sitting of an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts REST round I, giving RESIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Resits are second attempts at examinations previously failed, a British term.

clue.text: Haggle over uranium furnace

indicators.note: the word for haggle is laid over the chemical symbol, enclosing it

parts.note: to chaffer is to haggle
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Traders bargain over the price of uranium for a furnace.
explanation.definitionFit: A chauffer is a small portable heating stove or brazier.
